findings.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse() in CalendarService.ts returns the Zod safeParse result envelope ({success, data}) instead of the parsed credentials, so Google stores the envelope object as the credential key on every token refresh, breaking Google Calendar for all deployments

In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response without calling .json() or checking response.ok, while callers (Google reading res?.data, Hubspot reading .expires_in/.refresh_token, Zoho/ZohoCRM reading .data.error) expect provider-library shapes, causing TypeErrors or NaN expiry persisted

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to the literal "[object Object]" (duplicated key, second overriding first), so the schema validates nothing beyond access_token and never checks an expiry field

Zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId (the credential row id) instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, sent as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint, causing the parent app to look up/return tokens for the wrong user
Webhook secret in app-credential.ts is compared with !== (non-constant-time comparison), enabling timing attacks; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual

The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no shared secret/header), yet the endpoint returns OAuth tokens for arbitrary calcomUserId values, letting anyone who can reach it obtain any user's tokens
The app-credential webhook handler never checks req.method, so GET/PUT/DELETE etc. are all processed; a GET with no body hits z.parse(undefined) and throws

appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws an unhandled ZodError and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws on malformed ciphertext/JSON, both surfacing as 500s instead of 400s with meaningful messages; should use safeParse and try/catch

findFirst followed by create/update in the webhook is not atomic; two concurrent sync requests for the same (userId, appId) can both pass findFirst and create duplicate credentials — needs unique constraint/upsert or transaction
findFirst has no orderBy, so when a user holds multiple credentials for the same app an arbitrary one is selected and its keys are silently overwritten with no way to target the right credential

When credential sharing is enabled, the app-specific schema is replaced by minimumTokenResponseSchema and z.object strips unknown keys, e.g. Salesforce's refreshed instance_url/signature are dropped from the persisted key, losing the instance URL

A missing refresh_token is unconditionally replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted, permanently destroying the real refresh token for providers whose refresh response omits it if sync is later disabled

Salesforce CalendarService performs a token refresh plus credential DB write on every service instantiation (previously refresh was handled lazily by jsforce), adding an OAuth round-trip to every calendar operation and risking rate limits

The eagerly refreshed Salesforce token is only persisted; the returned jsforce.Connection is still constructed from the unchanged stale credentialKey values, so the new access token is never used by the current connection
if (response.statusText !== "OK") relies on the HTTP reason phrase, which is empty for HTTP/2 and can differ via proxies; should check response.ok instead

The previous console.error with the Zod error and raw Microsoft response was removed, and parseRefreshTokenResponse throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", losing all diagnostic detail for office365 refresh failures
The fetch to the sync endpoint has no timeout/AbortController; since token refresh runs during booking flows, a hanging parent endpoint stalls bookings

No tests added for the new webhook endpoint (auth, decryption, create/update/race paths), refreshOAuthTokens, or parseRefreshTokenResponse, which would have caught the Google key-envelope corruption and the "[object Object]" schema keys

The credential-sync integration contract is only described in code comments; the required CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT request/response format and the webhook's encrypted payload layout are not documented in .env.example or docs
The decrypted keys blob is persisted as the credential key without validating it against the app's expected credential schema, so a malformed parent payload silently poisons the integration

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirst followed by create/update in the webhook is not atomic; two concurrent sync requests for the same (userId, appId) can both pass findFirst and create duplicate credentials — needs unique constraint/upsert or transaction

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then conditionally calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` or `prisma.credential.create(...)`. This is a classic check-then-act race: two concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe no existing credential and both attempt `create`, leading to either duplicate rows (if no unique constraint exists) or a unique-constraint violation/500 (if such a constraint exists). The diff shows no transaction or `upsert`/unique-guard handling in this endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirst has no orderBy, so when a user holds multiple credentials for the same app an arbitrary one is selected and its keys are silently overwritten with no way to target the right credential

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the code uses `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` with no `orderBy`, then updates the found credential’s `key`. If the database can contain multiple credentials matching `(userId, appId)`, `findFirst` can select an arbitrary row and the update would overwrite that row’s keys. However, the diff does not show the Prisma schema/constraints, so it’s not verifiable from this diff alone that multiple such credentials are possible in practice; it’s an important edge-case/data-model assumption created by this change rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When credential sharing is enabled, the app-specific schema is replaced by minimumTokenResponseSchema and z.object strips unknown keys, e.g. Salesforce's refreshed instance_url/signature are dropped from the persisted key, losing the instance URL

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, the code validates the refresh response using `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the app-specific schema. `minimumTokenResponseSchema` only requires `access_token` and (attempts to) allow an expiry number, and Zod `z.object(...)` will strip unknown keys by default. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the persisted credential key is built from `accessTokenParsed.data` (`{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }`), so any Salesforce-specific fields returned on refresh (e.g., `instance_url`, `signature`) are dropped from the stored credential when the minimum schema path is taken, which matches the finding’s data-loss concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService performs a token refresh plus credential DB write on every service instantiation (previously refresh was handled lazily by jsforce), adding an OAuth round-trip to every calendar operation and risking rate limits

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an unconditional refresh-token request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)`) and then updates the credential in the DB (`prisma.credential.update(...)`) before constructing/returning the `jsforce.Connection`. This means every time the CalendarService is instantiated it will incur an OAuth round-trip and DB write, which is a significant architectural/performance change and can increase token-refresh traffic (and thus rate-limit risk) across calendar operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The previous console.error with the Zod error and raw Microsoft response was removed, and parseRefreshTokenResponse throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", losing all diagnostic detail for office365 refresh failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the prior `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` failure path that logged `tokenResponse.error` and the raw `responseJson` via `console.error(...)` was removed. It now calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which on parse failure throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`), losing the detailed Zod error and Microsoft response payload that previously aided diagnosing Office365 refresh failures. This is an observability/regression concern rather than a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The fetch to the sync endpoint has no timeout/AbortController; since token refresh runs during booking flows, a hanging parent endpoint stalls bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the code calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no `AbortController`/timeout. This means the awaiting code paths that refresh tokens (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Webex/etc. now routed through `refreshOAuthTokens`) can hang indefinitely if the parent endpoint stalls. The diff doesn’t prove this occurs specifically “during booking flows,” but the lack of timeout on a network call introduced by this PR is a concrete, actionable robustness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests added for the new webhook endpoint (auth, decryption, create/update/race paths), refreshOAuthTokens, or parseRefreshTokenResponse, which would have caught the Google key-envelope corruption and the "[object Object]" schema keys

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new logic without adding any accompanying test files: a new webhook endpoint `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` (auth via header secret, Zod parsing, decryption/JSON.parse, prisma create/update), plus new shared OAuth helpers `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, and integrates them across multiple apps’ token-refresh flows (Google, O365, Zoom, etc.). The PR diff shows no new/modified test coverage for these new code paths. While the finding’s references to specific past failures (“Google key-envelope corruption” and "[object Object]" schema keys) aren’t directly verifiable from the diff, the core issue—missing tests for newly added nontrivial behavior introduced here—is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The credential-sync integration contract is only described in code comments; the required CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT request/response format and the webhook's encrypted payload layout are not documented in .env.example or docs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new env vars in `.env.example` (CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME, CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY) but does not document the actual integration contract (endpoint request/response expectations or webhook payload format) there or anywhere else in the diff. The only guidance is inline comments in code, e.g. `refreshOAuthTokens` (“Customize the payload… response should only contain the access token and expiry date”) and the webhook handler schema/decryption logic in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` (expects `{ userId, appSlug, keys }` where `keys` is AES256-encrypted JSON). This is a concrete documentation gap created by the change, but not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The decrypted keys blob is persisted as the credential key without validating it against the app's expected credential schema, so a malformed parent payload silently poisons the integration

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse`d and written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` without any validation against the target app’s expected credential schema (only `appStoreMetadata` is looked up for `slug`/`type`). This allows malformed or unexpected key shapes from the parent app to be persisted, potentially breaking downstream integrations that assume a specific credential structure.
